page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel Xeon 6448H processor featuring 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz and lacks hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.25 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, offering 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier performance in specific workloads, particularly LLM inference. For a small 135M parameter model, prompt processing reaches 13631.52 tokens per second, while text generation achieves 610.8 tokens per second. For a medium 7B parameter model, prompt processing registers at 6293.73 tokens per second, with text generation at 153.1 tokens per second. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also ranks in the top tier at 15.59 GB/sec. In contrast, standard CPU compute and memory metrics fall into the average range, with a PassMark CPU score of 40930.36 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 34834.61.

This server offers high resource density by pairing a professional-grade GPU with a substantial 180.0 GB memory footprint and local NVMe storage. The qualitative cost efficiency is highly favorable for specialized AI inference tasks, where the GPU architecture delivers top-tier token throughput relative to the allocated 16 vCPUs. However, a key tradeoff is the moderate 2.0 GHz CPU clock speed and average general-purpose compute performance, indicating that workloads relying heavily on raw single-core CPU speed rather than GPU acceleration may not fully leverage this hardware profile.

Based on the hardware configuration and benchmark results, this server is designed for machine learning inference, specifically medium-sized LLM deployment, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated rendering. It is also suitable for database operations and data decompression tasks that benefit from the 1200 GB NVMe SSD and 180.0 GB of RAM.
